explanations: There is none. onBatch runs messages concurrently, which looks risky, but TripSequencer.handle chains each event onto the previous promise for the same tripId, so load/apply/save for one trip never interleave while different trips still run in parallel. Within a trip, events are only applied when their seq is exactly lastSeq + 1; later events wait in the pending buffer, and events with seq <= lastSeq (duplicates or redeliveries) are skipped. The chain uses a catch-wrapped promise so one failure does not poison later events, and the map entry is removed only if it is still the latest link.

A new trip starts at lastSeq 0, so seq 2 and 3 are buffered (applied stays false, no save) and onGap is called. When seq 1 arrives, the while loop applies 1, then the buffered 2 and 3, and saves once with lastSeq 3. Nothing is dropped since all seqs are above lastSeq.

process checks event.seq <= state.lastSeq and returns immediately, so handle resolves and onMessage acks. It is not buffered (only seqs above lastSeq are), state is not rewritten, and no error is thrown.

onBatch uses Promise.all, so messages start together, but handle keys its promise chain by tripId: different trips have independent chains and overlap, while events for the same trip wait for the previous link. Nothing nacks extra messages per trip.
